aboutH2: Gobind Wellness: in-home outpatient addiction program in South Surrey
intro: Gobind Wellness is a private addiction counselling and recovery coaching practice in South Surrey, run by addictions counsellor and recovery coach Bobby Bains. It has an office in Suite 300 at 15300 Croydon Drive, but most of the work happens in clients' homes. There are no treatment beds. The core service is an outpatient program you do while living at home and, often, while still working.

That program runs for 10 consecutive days and 30 hours: a two-hour one-to-one session each day, then a one-hour evening community support meeting that Bobby attends with you. People who need closer supervision can ask about a 30-day live-in option, where a recovery specialist stays with them at home or in Gobind Wellness accommodation. It is supervised support rather than a licensed residential program, and it does not include medical detox.

pillars.title: Ten days of treatment at your kitchen table
pillars.body: The 10-day program is built on the idea that you learn more by facing your triggers where they actually happen. Bobby comes to your home in Surrey, White Rock, Langley or Delta, or you meet at the Croydon Drive office, for two hours each day. Early days set up a plan and look at the wellness wheel. The middle days go through your life story, fears, anger and resentments, and later days add meditation, amends and boundaries. Every evening ends with a community support meeting, so by day 10 you already know a few local groups.

pillars.title: What the 30-day live-in option really is
pillars.body: The 30-day live-in program puts a Gobind Wellness recovery specialist with you around the clock for a month, in your own home or in one of the practice's accommodations. It adds random testing, daily exercise, meal prep, group and one-to-one sessions, meetings and family support. The website does not say where its accommodations are, so ask. This is not a licensed residential treatment centre and has no doctors or nurses on staff, so anyone who may go through serious withdrawal should talk to a physician first.

pillars.title: An aftercare plan built during the program
pillars.body: Gobind Wellness does not treat the last day as the end. By day 10 you should have an aftercare plan that includes regular meetings, a sponsor and a home group, a daily routine and a journal you have been keeping. Families take part on the final day, and phone support for you and your relatives continues afterwards. There are in-person check-ins at one, three and six months of sobriety, and you can call the 24-hour contact number when things get hard.

overview: Bobby Bains founded Gobind Wellness in South Surrey and also sees clients from a second office in Calgary. His bio describes losing a business and his family to drinking before he got help, and the program pages say he has 11 years of sobriety. He studied psychology and health sciences at Simon Fraser University and holds a life coaching certificate from Erickson College. The website does not list a registration with a regulatory body.

The work mixes addictions counselling, which looks at why someone drinks or uses, with recovery coaching, which deals with routine and accountability. Bobby also covers anxiety, depression and anger, plus practical areas such as fitness, nutrition, sleep, relationships and work. The spiritual side is described as mindfulness and awareness rather than religion.

faqIntro: Answers come from Gobind Wellness's own website and public listings. Still unsure? Call, it's free and confidential.

faqs.q: Is Gobind Wellness a residential rehab?
faqs.a: No. Gobind Wellness is a private outpatient counselling and recovery coaching practice in South Surrey, and its main 10-day program takes place in your home or at its office while you keep living at home. It also offers a 30-day live-in option, where a recovery specialist stays with you in your home or in one of Gobind Wellness's accommodations. That option is supervised support, not a licensed residential treatment facility.

You spend 10 consecutive days with counsellor Bobby Bains, about three hours a day and 30 hours in total. Each day has a two-hour one-to-one session at your home or the office, followed by a one-hour evening community support meeting. The days cover triggers, your life story, resentments and amends, meditation and a new daily routine, and day 10 is a family day where the aftercare plan is shared with your relatives.

faqs.q: How much does Gobind Wellness cost?
faqs.a: Single counselling or recovery coaching sessions cost $190 an hour, in person or by Zoom or phone. The 10-hour online program is listed at $1,800 on the service fees page. Rates for the 10-day in-person program and the 30-day live-in program are not published, so you need to call for a quote. All sessions and programs are paid at the time of booking.

No. Gobind Wellness does not offer medical detox, and its website says its staff are not doctors. It asks clients to see their family physician before starting so a doctor can plan any withdrawal care, which might include medication. If you drink or use heavily every day, medically supervised withdrawal management through Fraser Health or a private detox may be needed first.

faqs.q: Is Gobind Wellness covered by insurance or Fraser Health?
faqs.a: It is a private-pay service and is not publicly funded through Fraser Health. Gobind Wellness does not bill insurers directly. You pay first and can submit your receipts to your extended health plan, so check with your insurer if it covers sessions with an addictions counsellor or recovery coach.

Bobby Bains is the founder of Gobind Wellness and leads its 10-day program as addictions counsellor and recovery coach. His bio says he studied psychology and health sciences at Simon Fraser University and earned a life coaching certificate from Erickson College, and the program pages say he has 11 years of sobriety. The website does not list a registration with a counselling regulator or professional association, so ask about credentials if that matters to you or your insurer.

Most in-person sessions take place in the client's home anywhere in Surrey and the Lower Mainland. The office is in Suite 300 at 15300 Croydon Drive in South Surrey, about 45 minutes by car from downtown Vancouver and 10 minutes from White Rock. Bobby will also travel to clients elsewhere in Canada, with added charges outside the Lower Mainland and Calgary.

Yes. Family meetings are offered on the first day, partners and relatives are welcome on day 6, and day 10 is a family day built around the aftercare plan. Ongoing phone support for both the client and the family continues after the 10 days. Single family coaching sessions can also be booked.

faqs.q: What support is there after the 10 days?
faqs.a: Each client leaves with an aftercare plan built during the program. It includes community meetings, an introduction to a sponsor and a home group, a 24-hour contact number and in-person check-ins at the one, three and six month sobriety marks. Clients can keep booking counselling or coaching sessions after that.

faqs.q: Does Gobind Wellness offer services in Punjabi or for South Asian families?
faqs.a: The website does not describe a program designed for a particular culture or language, and it lists English for services. One client testimonial on the site mentions that Bobby Bains speaks Punjabi and that this helped her father. If language matters for you or a family member, ask when you call.

Call 778-868-0468 for a free 15-minute consultation, then choose whether sessions will be at home or in the office. You book the start date online and pay at booking, and the website says most people can begin within a few days. Programs can be rescheduled once but are not refundable.
